event_name: Finnmark witch prosecution begins at Vardø
significance: Systematic witch prosecution began in Finnmark, Norway, around 1620 with major trials at Vardø, continuing until 1692 and resulting in approximately 91 executions from a population of roughly 3,000 — the highest per-capita execution rate in Europe; the prosecution specifically targeted Sámi noaidi tradition alongside Norwegian-speaking communities, making it a distinctive case of colonially inflected witch-hunting.
source_method: Finnmark county court records; analyzed in Ankarloo and Henningsen, Early Modern European Witchcraft (1990) and Levack, The Witch-Hunt in Early Modern Europe (2006)
